{
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "title": "1. Protein preparation or assay conditions account for much of the activity difference",
      "question_and_explanation": "Does pig ADA2 remain less active when equivalent preparations are compared? The reported difference lacks effect size and assay details (CTX-01). Different signal-peptide annotations and glycosylation-site annotations (CTX-03), together with uncertainty about the actual pig construct (CTX-06), make processing and preparation important first explanations. As a general biochemical possibility, unequal amounts of correctly folded, processed protein could mimic an intrinsic catalytic difference. Under this hypothesis, both free-adenosine activity and other functions could remain intact in appropriately prepared pig ADA2.",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": ["CTX-01", "CTX-03", "CTX-06"],
      "conflicting_evidence_ids": [],
      "evidence_notes": "These records establish uncertainty, not a demonstrated preparation defect. Annotated glycosylation sites do not establish glycan occupancy in the tested proteins. No supplied observation rules out an intrinsic species difference.",
      "alternative_explanation": "Pig ADA2 has intrinsically different substrate recognition or catalytic behavior even when folding, processing, protein amount, and assay conditions are matched.",
      "proposed_test": "Verify the actual expression constructs, then compare independently prepared human and pig ADA2 made in the same expression system with comparable tag handling and purification. Measure adenosine disappearance and inosine formation across substrate concentrations and a shared range of assay conditions. In parallel, assess protein amount, integrity, mature termini, glycosylation, folding, oligomeric state, and zinc occupancy. If one preparation feature tracks activity, vary that feature independently rather than attributing causality to the initial comparison.",
      "predicted_outcome_if_true": "The activity gap substantially narrows after correcting preparation differences or choosing conditions that support both proteins. Activity tracks protein quality, processing, or assay conditions more strongly than species identity.",
      "falsifying_outcome": "A reproducible activity gap persists across independent preparations after protein quality, processing, amount, zinc occupancy, assembly, and assay conditions have been assessed and comparably controlled.",
      "controls_and_feasibility": "Include no-enzyme and mock-purification controls, product standards, a human ADA2 reference preparation, and independent protein batches. Normalize to quantified intact protein and report remaining uncertainty about the catalytically competent fraction. Expression, purification, chromatography, and relevant core characterization are supported by CTX-08, CTX-09, and CTX-10; specific scheduling and costs are not provided.",
      "next_decision": "If matching preparations removes the gap, identify the responsible preparation variable before pursuing species-specific mutations. If the gap persists, prioritize intrinsic kinetics and assembly tests. If results vary by batch without an identifiable cause, improve preparation reproducibility before interpreting biological differences.",
      "added_value_from_computation": "No computational evidence was supplied. This experiment comes from the background uncertainties; CTX-03 specifically adds processing and glycosylation checks, and CTX-06 adds construct verification. The causal effects proposed for folding, zinc occupancy, and assay conditions are general biochemical reasoning.",
      "confidence": "low"
    },
    {
      "title": "2. Pig ADA2 has altered substrate preference, with DNA-associated activity potentially preserved",
      "question_and_explanation": "Could pig ADA2 handle free adenosine poorly while retaining activity on deoxyadenosine within DNA? Lower free-adenosine activity is reported in CTX-01, whereas DNA interactions and DNA-associated deamination were reported for ADA2 in CTX-04. A species-dependent change in substrate recognition is therefore testable, but neither a responsible substitution nor preserved pig DNA activity is established.",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": ["CTX-01", "CTX-02", "CTX-04"],
      "conflicting_evidence_ids": [],
      "evidence_notes": "CTX-04 motivates a second substrate class; it does not demonstrate that pig ADA2 binds or edits DNA. There is no supplied alignment or pig structure supporting a particular residue-level mechanism.",
      "alternative_explanation": "Pig ADA2 has a general loss of catalytic competence rather than selective loss of free-adenosine activity. Alternatively, apparent DNA activity could arise from contaminants or free nucleosides rather than modification within DNA.",
      "proposed_test": "Using quality-matched preparations, compare concentration-dependent free-adenosine kinetics with separate measurements of DNA binding, DNA-associated deoxyadenosine-to-deoxyinosine conversion, and DNA cleavage. Verify that any conversion product derives from the DNA fraction rather than free nucleosides. Include free deoxyadenosine as an additional comparator to help distinguish nucleoside chemistry from recognition of a DNA context.",
      "predicted_outcome_if_true": "Pig ADA2 shows a smaller deficit relative to human ADA2 for DNA-associated deamination than for free-adenosine turnover. Preserved DNA binding alone would support retained interaction capacity, but would not establish preserved editing.",
      "falsifying_outcome": "Pig ADA2 loses DNA-associated deamination to a similar or greater extent than free-adenosine turnover under validated, matched conditions. Failure to reproduce DNA-associated conversion with the human reference would make the pig comparison inconclusive rather than falsify it.",
      "controls_and_feasibility": "Include human ADA2, no-protein and mock-purification controls, independent protein batches, appropriate analytical standards, and checks for contaminating deaminases or nucleases. Measure DNA integrity separately from base conversion. Match protein amount, processing, glycosylation, folding, and assembly, and test shared assay conditions. Purification and mass-spectrometry access are supported by CTX-08 through CTX-10, but a validated DNA-editing assay is not documented.",
      "next_decision": "If selective preservation is observed, verify it with an orthogonal readout before mapping sequence determinants or testing TLR9-related cellular consequences. If binding is retained without editing, pursue a noncatalytic interaction hypothesis instead. If both catalytic activities are impaired, investigate shared catalytic competence, zinc occupancy, or assembly.",
      "added_value_from_computation": "No computational evidence was supplied. CTX-04 changes the proposed experiment from a free-nucleoside assay alone to separate binding, editing, and cleavage measurements. Substrate selectivity and the free-deoxyadenosine comparator are general biochemical reasoning, not computed findings.",
      "confidence": "low"
    },
    {
      "title": "3. Altered dimer assembly reduces free-adenosine turnover while leaving interaction functions intact",
      "question_and_explanation": "Does pig ADA2 assemble differently, and does that account for reduced activity? Human ADA2 is a homodimer (CTX-02), but pig assembly in the laboratory preparations is unknown. General biochemical reasoning suggests that altered assembly could affect catalytic organization without abolishing a separate DNA- or partner-binding surface. Preserved binding or localization could be relevant to functions beyond free-adenosine turnover, but the pig disease phenotype alone does not identify such a function (CTX-07).",
      "supporting_evidence_ids": ["CTX-01", "CTX-02", "CTX-04"],
      "conflicting_evidence_ids": [],
      "evidence_notes": "The evidence establishes human dimerization, not an assembly defect in pig ADA2 or a requirement for dimerization in catalysis. This hypothesis is less directly supported than the need to control protein preparation.",
      "alternative_explanation": "Both orthologs form equivalent dimers, and the activity difference comes from local catalytic properties. Alternatively, apparent assembly differences reflect misfolding, aggregation, tags, glycosylation, or protein concentration rather than a native species difference.",
      "proposed_test": "Measure oligomeric state and free-adenosine turnover across matched protein concentrations and conditions, accounting for concentration-dependent assembly during the activity assay. Where feasible, compare well-characterized assembly states while checking folding and integrity. Measure DNA binding independently. Only if an assembly-dependent activity difference is found, test whether a controlled shift toward the human-like assembly state changes pig turnover without altering protein quality.",
      "predicted_outcome_if_true": "Pig ADA2 has a different assembly distribution, and its turnover per unit protein tracks the dimer fraction. Favoring the human-like assembly state increases pig activity. DNA binding can remain detectable in a low-turnover state.",
      "falsifying_outcome": "Both proteins show equivalent assembly under activity-assay conditions yet retain different turnover, or changing the pig dimer fraction leaves turnover unchanged after folding and protein amount are controlled. Loss of DNA binding would contradict the proposed preserved interaction, but not by itself the assembly mechanism.",
      "controls_and_feasibility": "Use human ADA2 as an assembly reference, independent preparations, matched tags and processing, aggregation and folding checks, and an orthogonal oligomerization measurement. DNA-binding controls should include unrelated nucleic-acid competitors to assess nonspecific association. CTX-08 and CTX-09 support protein characterization and FPLC; the exact available method for absolute oligomeric mass is not specified. Any use of the ADA2 aptamer from CTX-08 requires validating pig recognition first.",
      "next_decision": "If assembly causally tracks activity, investigate assembly determinants only after verifying and aligning the actual constructs. If assembly is equivalent, deprioritize this mechanism and focus on substrate handling. If DNA binding persists, consider cellular localization and TLR9-response tests with matched uptake, protein amount, and contamination controls; binding alone is not evidence of a preserved TLR9 function.",
      "added_value_from_computation": "No computational evidence was supplied. CTX-02 motivates the assembly measurement, and CTX-04 motivates an independent interaction readout. The assembly-to-catalysis connection is a general biochemical hypothesis; no interface residues or structural differences can be nominated from the supplied evidence.",
      "confidence": "low"
    }
  ],
  "overall_note": "Prioritize the matched-preparation comparison, incorporating oligomeric-state measurements where practical, before undertaking sequence swaps or animal experiments. The literature observations are explicitly provisional, and the reported activity difference lacks quantitative detail. No supplied sequence analysis or pig experimental structure justifies naming causal residues. DNA binding, DNA editing, DNA cleavage, localization, and TLR9 effects require distinct readouts; none is established as preserved in pig ADA2."
}
